olivia (csm): FYI Acme hitting intermittent failures during SDK onboarding, they see auth errors + timeouts in staging since last deploy
acme-dev@acme.com: seeing 2xx then sudden spikes to 5xx and some calls that look like expired tokens returned as 401s, not sure whether it's rate-limiting or token refresh race
onboard-bot: New onboarding ticket created: OB-4893 assigned to olivia (csm)
jules (solutions): can you paste a small curl or SDK log snippet? curious about headers and whether they rotate tokens per request
acme-dev@acme.com: here's a snippet from node SDK logs (sanitized):
```
[2025-06-02T14:12:03Z] POST /v1/generate 200
[2025-06-02T14:12:21Z] POST /v1/generate 503 {"error":"upstream timeout"}
[2025-06-02T14:12:21Z] POST /v1/generate 401 {"error":"invalid_token"}
[2025-06-02T14:12:27Z] POST /v1/generate 200
```
acme-dev@acme.com: also sometimes get this header back: `x-rw-req-remaining: 0` but it doesn't line up with their usage numbers
sam (eng): two quick checks: 1) are you using long-lived API key or short-lived token with refresh? 2) any outbound proxy or gateway that might be mutating Authorization header?
olivia (csm): Acme said they're using short-lived tokens issued by their auth server and they refresh every 45m via our SDK helper
jules (solutions): that refresh cadence is fine. common problem: multiple parallel requests triggering concurrent refresh and some still sent with old token -> 401s. SDK has a lock/mutex option to serialize refresh. what SDK version are you on?
acme-dev@acme.com: using `@redwood/sdk` 0.9.1
sam (eng): aha, 0.9.1 had optimistic refresh without a global lock. 0.9.3 added a refresh lock and jittered backoff for 429/503. can you upgrade to 0.9.3? also check that their refresh endpoint returns 200 consistently and low latency
ajules (solutions): also check client-side retry/backoff config. sample recommended pattern:
```
// pseudo
if (resp.status === 401) {
  await tokenRefreshLock.acquire()
  await refreshTokenIfExpired()
  tokenRefreshLock.release()
  retryRequestWithNewToken()
}
if (resp.status === 503 || resp.headers['x-rw-req-remaining'] === '0') {
  await backoff( jitteredDelay() )
}
```
acme-dev@acme.com: we do see spikes in latency to our token issuer during their peak tests - they run parallel 100s of requests during onboarding scripts
olivia (csm): sounds like two causes: token issuer latency causing more 401s and the SDK earlier version causing thundering herd on refresh. plan: recommend upgrade + temporary rate limit on their test runner and ensure refresh endpoint scaling
sam (eng): also check server-side logs for `auth: token_expired` vs `auth: invalid_token` to confirm race vs bad tokens. i can grep logs if you grant request id(s) from their failing calls
acme-dev@acme.com: giving two request ids: rq_7f9b2 and rq_7f9b8. attaching logs now
(onboard-bot): olivia added sam (eng) to OB-4893
sam (eng): thanks, I see both rq_* show token refresh in progress and several parallel requests with old token -> 401 then immediate success after refresh for later requests. also a few 503s where upstream worker timed out.
jules (solutions): next steps: 1) acme upgrades to SDK 0.9.3 (we'll give them a patch snippet), 2) add client-side refresh lock and exponential backoff, 3) throttle their onboarding runner to ~20 concurrent, 4) we monitor for 24h and revisit SLA/renewal risk if unresolved
olivia (csm): i'll send a short enablement doc and schedule a 30m call tomorrow to help them upgrade and test. also marking renewal risk as low for now but will watch usage patterns
acme-dev@acme.com: thanks team, started a canary upgrade to 0.9.3 on staging. will report back in ~1h after run
sam (eng): if they still see 503s after upgrade, we'll look at routing fallback and autoscale knobs on Dedicated pool. ping me with traces
jules (solutions): posted a quick diff for their app to add a refresh lock: https://internal.redwood.dev/solutions/OB-4893/refresh-lock-diff :thumbsup:
olivia (csm): thanks all :heart:
